results.summary_before: This design implements a single artificial neuron (perceptron) in pure combinational logic. It takes four binary inputs, each multiplied by a 2-bit weight, sums them, and compares the result to a configurable threshold to produce a binary output. Weights and threshold are set via input pins, making it fully reconfigurable without re-synthesis. The design includes a cocotb testbench and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This design is a digital bioimpedance demodulator that processes a 1-bit sigma-delta ADC input through eight cascaded I/Q stages, each halving the clock frequency, to produce 128 bits of I and Q data. The results are stored in a register and can be read either via a UART transmitter at 9600 baud on uio[0] or through a 16-to-1 multiplexer selected by ui[1:4] and output on uo[0:7]. It requires an external 1-bit signal source, such as a sigma-delta ADC, and a USB-UART adapter for serial readout. The design is notable for its very low resource implementation of bioimpedance analysis in GF180 technology, though no silicon test results are provided.

results.summary_before: The Acoustic Interferometer samples two PDM microphones, mixes the 1-bit streams with a 20 kHz complex tone, averages over 2^16 samples, and uses a CORDIC in vectoring mode to compute the phase difference between channels. The resulting 7-bit signed angle is shown as a one-hot value on an LED bar and also transmitted over UART for debugging. It is intended to run with a dedicated PMOD PCB carrying the microphones and LEDs, and a phone speaker playing a 20 kHz tone is used to verify that the LED bar tracks the direction of arrival. The design is written in Chisel and is notable for combining PDM capture, complex mixing, and CORDIC phase detection on a 1x2 tile.

results.summary_before: This design combines a sigma-delta DAC and a tracking-loop ADC, where the DAC's pulse-density output is filtered externally to produce an analog voltage and an off-chip comparator closes the ADC feedback loop. ADC readings are transmitted as hex-encoded ASCII over a UART at the clock rate, and a second 8-bit DAC is controlled by UART words received at one tenth of the clock rate. Testing requires an external comparator, resistors and capacitors to build the RC filters and feedback path. The project is notable for demonstrating mixed-signal conversion using only digital primitives plus a few passive components.

results.summary_before: This design generates the GPS C/A PRN sequences for PRN1 through PRN32 using two LFSRs built to the GPS ICD, with selected taps of the second LFSR combined with the first to produce the chosen code. The PRN index is selected on the input pins, and the G1, G2 and selected PRN outputs are exposed. Testing is done by selecting a PRN, resetting, and clocking while checking the output sequence against the expected pattern. No external hardware is needed, and the documentation is concise but adequate.
